about: avenDB's performance gates, held by scripts/ci/avendb-bench.mjs to the lines of crates/avendb/tests/bench_gates.rs and crates/avendb-server/tests/relay_bench.rs (the bench job of avendb-checks.yml). A gate missed fails the PR; a target is printed with whether it is met. Gates sit at the level reached on 2026-10-27 with headroom for a shared runner; raise one when the code reaches past it. The carriers' gates sit at under half of the first CI run's (2026-10-27: direct 582 edits/s, relay 710, a 1 MB/s link 93 edits/s at 0.56 of it, 1001 edits of 6 KB); draft_on_ratio_max (1.2) is null until Log::draft_on reads its log's index (claude/s-draft-on). The phone-class rows (WebAssembly in Chromium and WebKit) gate nothing yet. The index rows (index_sizes, parity_n: avendb-net's shelf_index_bench.rs, run with --index in the net test shard) gate counts, not only time: a view opened cold steps on no log edit and reads pages as the tree is deep (depth within the model's; a view's 50 rows the median open reads at most one page past the depth, the worst of 200 at most 6, as a page may hold few rows); 2026-10-27: 1M 3 deep, at most 7 pages, 81 KB; 10M 4, 8, 59 KB; 100M (by hand) 4, 7, 67 KB, built in 157 s; 49 index bytes/edit at each. The window rows (window_sizes: avendb-net's query_window_bench.rs, gate G1 of batch 5) open a named query end to end as Node::window does, cold: 2026-10-27, 1M 3 pages median, 5 at most, 55 KB, 50 rows, 0 log edits, 82 µs; 10M 4, 6, 61 KB, 100 µs; but the check that the index is of a prefix of the log hashes every id up to its stamp on each open, 38 ms at 1M and 405 ms at 10M, so window_at_n_p50_us (window plus that hash) misses its 5 ms on purpose until the log keeps its heads. The posts row (avendb's tests/posts_bench.rs, run in the core test shard with --posts) holds the Universe's query-posts (A3) to the same: a page off its cursor costs no more per edit of a post (it reads no history) and stays under 5 ms at 1M and 10M edits, from the slopes measured on small vaults (a Lab of 1M edits can't be written in a test). 2026-10-27, debug: 7.4 ms a page at 62 entries, 6.2 µs more per edit of a post, 4.4 per other entry held, so 96 ms at 1M and 0.9 s at 10M, 6 s and 61 s where every entry is a post: it walks every entry and each post's history. log_bytes_per_edit_max (3,585 on 2026-10-27: 244 bytes an edit, its id, one ML-DSA-65 signature an edit while S8 is off) catches growth; the target bytes_ratio_pg (log over Postgres's bytes/edit) needs S8's one signature a segment. The live rows (live_links: avendb-net's tests/sync_bench.rs, plan D3, batch 5's exit gates) hold a live edit's delay while a device catches up on a bulk of history, on a simulated calm link and a phone's (50 Mbit/s, 40 ms round trip, 1 % lost): p95 under 500 ms, none missing at 15 s, the catch-up using at least 80 % of a set-rate link, and at most 5 % of edits sent again. First run, 2026-10-27, calm, 3,000 edits: catch-up 14 s (215 edits/s), live p95 11.8 s during it (the iPhone's LIVE_WAIT case), 107 ms idle.
